Original_Text: GSC Mid Valley always gives a memorable childhood and teenage nostalgic feeling. Came here after many years, and it's good to see lots of changes have been done but looks like some touch-up need to be done. Yesterday (18/5), I came for Michael at the 6pm show with my family. My mum and aunty had leg issues, and when I approached the staff at the autogate, I asked if they could allow both of them inside first to sit. Immediately one of the staff went to find chairs for both of them. After that, there was a trainee even later to assist in taking the special lift for the wheelchair. Happy to see that all the staff were very helpful and understanding. Kudos for the whole team, including F&B. But for me, still feeling the parking and going to GSC in Mid Valley is still a challenge. Yesterday I parked at Zone 3; then parking at levels 4 & 5 will be ideal, and from the car lot, walk to the exit area heading to the shop (it depends on which side you are parking on; as for me, I need to cross to another side to exit to the shop). Overall good & happy to come back to GSC

The fries were unsalted and tasted stale, as though they had been sitting around for a long time. Even the ketchup had a strange taste. 2. The movie audio was terrible. Throughout the movie, the background music was so loud that we could barely hear the characters speaking. We ended up relying heavily on the subtitles just to follow the story. I approached an attendant to report the issue, but instead of looking into it, he repeatedly insisted that the problem was because I was seated in the last row. I regularly choose last-row seats at other cinemas and have never experienced anything like this before. When I asked whether the dialogue volume could be increased, his response was that if they did so, "people in the front wouldn't be able to hear the background music." That explanation made no sense. Surely hearing the dialogue is more important than hearing background music. He continued insisting that this was normal for back-row seating. To test his claim, my partner walked over to the middle section of the hall, and the audio was just as bad there. Clearly, the seating position was not the issue. The entire interaction felt dismissive, and I was left feeling as though my concerns were being brushed aside rather than taken seriously. Honestly, my TV at home provides clearer audio than this cinema. Had I known the experience would be this poor, I would have stayed home and watched Netflix instead. If all I wanted was loud background music, I could have spent my money attending an orchestra. 3. The reviews raise questions. A large number of the positive reviews appear to have been posted within a short period of time, which makes them look suspicious. Whether they are purchased reviews or staff-generated reviews, I cannot say. However, based on my experience, I find it difficult to believe that the overwhelmingly positive ratings accurately reflect the actual customer experience. I will not be returning. I genuinely feel sorry for moviegoers in Melaka if this is one of their main cinema options.
